text:
alex: Quick question — who should own the lifecycle hooks that affect route selection: the policy compiler or the runtime? Trying to pin down responsibilities for hotreloads and probe-driven adjustments.

mira: My quick take: compiler owns structural changes (graph shape, node types), runtime owns dynamic signals (probes, telemetry, short-lived overrides). :thinking:

ton y: We keep hitting races when a compiled rollout changes node ids while runtimes are still applying probe updates.

alex: Right — the bug last week was basically "compiler replaced node X with Y" while runtime tried to patch X's cache. We need clearer invariants.

mira: Proposal: two hook classes. 1) compile-time transforms (affect serialization + node schema). 2) runtime adapters (only mutate runtime-local state, no schema changes). Document the invariant: runtime adapters must never rely on stable node ids unless guarded by compatibility metadata.

sam: ops-bot: deploy finished: policy-compiler v2.3 -> prod (canary 10%) <https://ci/redwood/12345> :white_check_mark:

tony: To make that precise: runtime adapters can add per-route hints and cache entries, but must be namespaced by a runtime-probe-id and a TTL. If compiler changes shape, the namespaced keys are ignored.

alex: That avoids stale cross-version cache pollution. How do we signal compatibility from compiler -> runtimes?

mira: Add a "shape_version" and a small capability bitmap in the compiled artifact. Runtime advertises supported capabilities. Compiler emits fallback annotations for unknown capabilities.

alex: Sketch config example:

```json
{"route_graph_v": 12,
 "capabilities": ["late_bind_probes","kv_namespacing_v1"],
 "fallback_policy": "fallback-to-compat-v11"
}
```

tony: That helps. Also we should define semantic guarantees for runtime "soft-eval" hooks: they can observe telemetry and suggest a route, but final decision must be rechecked against compiled guard rails. In short: runtime suggestions are advisory unless they pass guard checks.

alex: Agree. Need to record idempotency and determinism constraints so the distributed decision is stable under retries.

mira: Operationally: require the runtime to emit a decision delta and a decision_proof (compact fingerprint) that compiler can map back to original node. If mapping fails, runtime must fall back to default route.

sam: ops-bot: incident-345 follow-up: add a check in policy-service that rejects artifacts with incompatible capability bits.

tony: One more tradeoff: adding proofs increases artifact size / latency. We should keep proofs tiny (e.g., 64-bit fingerprints) and accept probabilistic collisions with safe fallbacks.

alex: Sounds reasonable. Action items:
- mira: draft RFC defining hook classes, compat envelope, and proof format.
- tony: prototype namespacing + TTL semantics in runtime adapter.
- alex: add rollout checklist to prevent node-id swaps during canary windows.

mira: I'll start the RFC. Put it in docs/rfcs and ping arch-review.

alex: Thanks — please include a couple small examples for existing policies (latency-first, cost-first) so we can validate. :thumbsup:

mira: Will do. Filing follow-up RFC now (WIP).
